title: Platform Resilience Scenario Catalog & Verification Kit
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This document is a curated catalog of resilience scenarios and a verification kit for platform teams to validate operational readiness. It standardizes: scenario definitions, acceptance criteria, synthetic test harnesses, required dashboard panels and alert checks, runbook cross-references, and a scoring rubric for post-exercise retrospectives.

Audience:
- Platform SREs and Operators
- Platform engineers responsible for runtime, allocator, cache, and routing subsystems
- Engineering managers planning gamedays or quarterly resilience objectives

Goals:
- Provide repeatable, measurable scenarios that exercise cross-service failure modes for LLM inference workloads
- Reduce ambiguity during gamedays by supplying concrete metrics, PromQL queries, and remediation playbooks
- Enable a lightweight verification pass for each scenario (pass/fail + remediation checklist)

How to use this kit (high level):
1) Select scenarios aligned to the scope (regional, multi-region, or single-service).
2) Wire up the supplied dashboard panels and ensure synthetic generators are available in the test namespace.
3) Run the scenario under controlled blast radius (canary tenant or synthetic-tenants 1..N).
4) Observe verification checklist and record scores.
5) Open issues for failures and schedule follow-up fixes.

Scenario catalog (short form):
- Scenario A: Prefix-cache severe miss storm
  - Target systems: kv-prefix-cache, router, model-runtime
  - Blast radius: single region, synthetic-tenants=50
  - Goal: Verify cache prefetch heuristics and eviction safety under sustained cold prefixes
  - Acceptance criteria: P99 token-generation latency for synthetic workload remains <= 350ms for 95% of requests; cache write-error-rate < 0.1%; no allocator OOMs
  - Key metrics / PromQL examples:
    - prefix_cache_miss_rate = sum(rate(prefix_cache_miss_total[1m]))
    - model_p99_latency = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - Verification steps:
    1. Start synthetic generator: kubectl -n resilience-test run prefix-storm --image=ghcr.io/redwood/tests:synthetic -- /usr/local/bin/prefetch-storm --tenants 50 --rate 200
    2. Monitor dashboards: Prefetch > Cache Overview, Runtime P99 panel, Allocator OOM events panel
    3. If model_p99_latency > 350ms sustained for 5m, trigger graceful-eviction-runbook and scale burst pool by +20%
  - Related runbooks: runbooks/predictive-scale-and-eviction-playbook-2026.json

- Scenario B: Regional routing gateway partial outage + fallback misconfiguration
  - Target systems: regional-router, routing-gateway, global-failover
  - Blast radius: region-a traffic (10% production-equivalent) routed to fallback
  - Goal: Validate routing policies, fallbacks, and canary rollback behavior for model variants
  - Acceptance criteria: traffic reroute completes within 45s, error-rate to host-model <= 2%, successful model-variant fallback invoked for >= 99% of degraded host requests
  - Key checks:
    - promql: increase in region_routing_failures = sum(rate(router_request_errors_total{region="region-a"}[1m]))
    - console check: verify canary traffic percentage and rollback flag in rollout service
  - Verification steps:
    1. Inject 503 on routing-gateway in region-a: kubectl -n chaos exec -- bash -c 'tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 600ms && pkill -f routing-gateway'
    2. Validate: alert "regional-fallback-initiated" fires; downstream model-variant metrics show fallback invocation
    3. Revert test and confirm rollback path clears metrics within 10m
  - Related pages: ../systems-and-services/regional-fallback-zero-trust-routing-playbook-2026.json

- Scenario C: Token-cost spike from unbounded sampling loop
  - Target systems: api-gateway, usage-metering, billing-pipeline
  - Blast radius: single customer sandbox -> billable tokens spike
  - Goal: Validate soft-quota enforcement, cost alerts, and automated short-circuiting to safe-policy model
  - Acceptance criteria: usage soft-quota throttles at configured threshold (e.g., 1M tokens/hour), token-billing lag < 10 minutes for alerting, cost-alert route escalates to oncall within 2 minutes
  - Verification steps:
    1. Synthetic user: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer synthetic' -d @large-sample-prompt.json --repeat 5000
    2. Monitor billing: sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[5m])) by (tenant_id)
    3. Confirm automated safe-policy model swapped for tenant via feature-flag and throttle headers returned

- Scenario D: Allocator fragmentation and node drain during rolling kernel update
  - Target systems: allocator-service, gpu-pool-manager, node-exporter
  - Blast radius: multi-az, controlled maintenance window
  - Goal: Ensure continuous throughput with minimal P95 increase during rolling kernel upgrades on GPU nodes
  - Acceptance criteria: P95 latency < baseline*1.4; eviction rate under emergency eviction threshold; tenant SLA violations < 1%
  - Steps:
    1. Schedule: maintenance window and operator oncall present
    2. Execute live-shrink with drain script: ./tools/gpu-drain --pool=dedicated-1 --max-evict=3 --grace-period=300s
    3. Observe allocator_rebalance_events and pre-warm burst pool before drain completes

- Scenario E: Telemetry fanout blackhole (explainability and fail-open behavior)
  - Target systems: telemetry-proxy, observability-fanout, slo-evaluator
  - Goal: Validate observability-stub behavior and ensure SLIs degrade gracefully while alerting is noisy-resistant
  - Acceptance criteria: telemetry buffering keeps 30m of backlog; alert suppression rules kick in when signal-loss is predictable; critical SLOs still have alternate sources for verification (synthetic canaries)

Verification kit components (what to deploy):
- Synthetic generators: image ghcr.io/redwood/tests:synthetic with subcommands: prefetch-storm, token-bomb, endpoint-reroute
- Canary namespace: resilience-test (Kubernetes) with RBAC read-only access to monitoring namespace
- Dashboard bundle: JSON export for Grafana panels (panels included: Runtime P99, Cache Hit/Miss, Allocator Evictions, Token Rate by Tenant, Routing Error Heatmap, Telemetry Backlog)
- Alert set: companion Alertmanager rules for each scenario and a gating rule that prevents false-positive pager escalation during known gameday windows

Sample PromQL and alert rule snippets (copyable):
- Model p99 latency (panel): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
- Token-rate tenant alert (rule): |
  - expr: sum by (tenant_id) (rate(tokens_emitted_total[5m])) > 1000000
  - for: 10m
  - labels: {severity: "page", category: "cost"}
  - annotations: {summary: "High token issuance for tenant {{ $labels.tenant_id }}"}
Gameday run checklist (operational):
1. Pre-flight (24h): schedule oncall, coordinate with product owners, lock change freeze, whitelist test tenant IDs, provision resilience-test namespace
2. 0-15m: baseline capture (collect 30m baseline metrics if possible)
3. 15-60m: execute scenario steps in the documented order; keep blast radius conservative for first run
4. 60-90m: execute verification checklist and record metrics into the standard gameday template
5. Post-mortem: open retro issue with pass/fail and remediation owner assigned within 48h

Scoring rubric (example):
- Pass: acceptance criteria met without emergency interventions (score 3)
- Partial: acceptance criteria met after operator intervention that did not cause customer-visible degradation (score 2)
- Fail: acceptance criteria not met or caused customer-visible SLA breaches (score 1)

Operational artifacts and templates (where to store):
- Dashboard bundle: dashboards/resilience-kit/{scenario-name}.json
- Synthetic job definitions: infra/k8s/resilience-test/jobs/{job}.yaml
- Gameday report template: templates/gameday-report.md

Example synthetic job YAML (deploy into resilience-test namespace):
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: token-bomb
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: token-bomb
        image: ghcr.io/redwood/tests:synthetic
        args: ["token-bomb", "--tenants=1", "--rate=1000", "--duration=900"]
      restartPolicy: Never

(Place the above YAML under infra/k8s/resilience-test/jobs/token-bomb.yaml)

Post-exercise retro template (capture):
- Scenario executed:
- Start/End times:
- Blast radius:
- Observed vs expected: (metrics, graphs attach)
- Operator interventions (what and why):
- Root cause analysis (if failure):
- Action items (owner + ETA):
- Final score (Pass/Partial/Fail):

Maintenance and ownership:
- Owner: Platform Resilience Squad (rotating oncall: platform-resilience@redwood.ai)
- Quarterly cadence: run at least 2 scenarios per quarter; rotate ownership of scenario leads between allocator, routing, and telemetry teams
- Health metrics: number of open action items older than 30d; percentage of scenarios with verification documentation updated in last 6 months

Appendix: quick command reference
- Start synthetic prefetch storm (k8s): kubectl -n resilience-test run prefetch-storm --image=ghcr.io/redwood/tests:synthetic -- /usr/local/bin/prefetch-storm --tenants 50 --rate 200
- Query top token emitters (Prometheus): topk(10, sum by (tenant_id) (rate(tokens_emitted_total[5m])))
- Grafana import: grafana-cli --homepath /var/lib/grafana plugins install <dashboard-plugin> && grafana-cli --import dashboards/resilience-kit/prefetch-cache-overview.json

Contacts and escalation map:
- Platform Resilience Squad: platform-resilience@redwood.ai (primary)
- Allocator oncall: allocator-oncall@redwood.ai
- Routing oncall: routing-oncall@redwood.ai
- Observability: obs-platform@redwood.ai
